text: **Work Summary – Soo-jin Park (Developer)**  During this reporting period, I focused on backend stability and feature delivery for the authentication and user-profile services. My primary achievement was refactoring the legacy session-handling module into a token-based system using industry-standard JWT practices. This reduced average login latency by 18% and eliminated recurring 500 errors caused by race conditions in concurrent session updates.  I also implemented a database indexing strategy for high-traffic user queries, cutting read times for profile endpoints from 120ms to 45ms under peak load. Collaborating with the QA team, I wrote automated integration tests covering 85% of the new auth flows, which caught two critical edge cases before production deployment.  On the frontend side, I assisted in migrating the dashboard’s state management to a more predictable reducer pattern. This improved developer debugging efficiency and reduced UI flickering during data refresh cycles. I also documented the new architecture in the internal wiki, including sequence diagrams and environment variable guidelines, to facilitate onboarding for two new junior developers.  Challenges this month included a third-party API rate-limit incident that caused intermittent sync failures. I led the investigation, implemented exponential backoff and retry logic, and added proactive alerting metrics to prevent recurrence. The fix has held steady for two consecutive weeks without incident.  Looking ahead, I will prioritize performance optimization for the notification queue and begin a proof-of-concept for server-side caching of frequently accessed user metadata. My time management has been solid, though I aim to improve code review turnaround by proposing a weekly pair-review slot with the frontend team.  Overall, I met my sprint commitments, improved system resilience, and contributed to team knowledge sharing. I remain committed to clean code principles and measurable impact. **Work Summary – Soo-jin Park**  Today, I focused on optimizing the authentication flow for our DID-based wallet integration. Specifically, I refactored the key derivation module to reduce latency during credential presentation and added unit tests for edge cases involving expired verifiable credentials. I also reviewed the privacy-preserving selective disclosure logic, ensuring that only the minimal required claims are shared with relying parties.  On decentralized identity, I believe the core promise lies in user-centric control, not just technical abstraction. However, true privacy requires deliberate design: avoiding correlation vectors, implementing data minimization by default, and ensuring revocation mechanisms do not leak metadata. The current ecosystem still over-indexes on convenience at the expense of anonymity, and we must push back on that in our implementations.
